title: (fix) O3-6102: Fetch all pages of lab orders in the worklist
body: ## Requirements - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration. - [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary The lab worklist was only reading the first page of results from `/ws/rest/v1/order`. The server returns 50 orders per page by default, so when the selected date range had more than 50 orders, the older ones never showed up in the table. Narrowing the date range made them appear again, which is confusing and can leave lab staff unaware of orders that are still waiting to be picked up. This PR makes `useLabOrders` follow the `next` links from the server until all pages are loaded. Filtering, grouping by patient and table pagination now work on the full list of orders. A few notes: - I kept the existing `useSWR` call and only changed the fetcher. `useInvalidateLabOrders` and the add results action refresh the list by matching the SWR cache key, and that keeps working this way. I didn't use `useOpenmrsFetchAll` because it is built on `useSWRInfinite`, and those cache keys are skipped by a filter based `mutate`, so the list would stop refreshing after pick up, reject or result entry. - The next page URL uses the current host and protocol, the same way the framework handles it, so it still works behind a proxy and in local dev. - When a date range has more than 50 orders you will now see one extra request per page in the Network tab (`startIndex=50`, `startIndex=100`, ...). For 50 or fewer orders nothing changes. - Added unit tests for a single page, multiple pages, and the next page URL. ### How to test 1. Pick a date range that has more than 50 lab orders. 2. Go to Laboratory > Tests ordered. 3. Before this change the Tests ordered count stops at 50 and older patients are missing. After this change the count shows all orders and the older patients appear. 4. In the Network tab you should see the follow up requests with `startIndex`. ## Screenshots ## Related Issue https://issues.openmrs.org/browse/O3-6102 ## Other This paging behaviour was already there in v1.5.2, so it's not a regression from the current release candidate.

- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

This PR replaces `jwalton/gh-docker-logs` in the E2E workflow with the org's shared [`capture-docker-logs`](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-contrib-gha-workflows/blob/main/.github/actions/capture-docker-logs/action.yml) action from [openmrs-contrib-gha-workflows#60](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-contrib-gha-workflows/pull/60). It does the same thing: it writes each container's logs to `logs/<container name>.log` for the upload step that follows.

`jwalton/gh-docker-logs` declares the Node 20 runtime, which GitHub [removed from hosted runners](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/) on September 23. Runners now force it onto Node 24 with a deprecation warning. It hasn't had a release since v2.2.2 in January 2024, so there's no Node 24 version to upgrade to.

title: (chore) Share SWR through module federation
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [ ] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Adds `swr` to `peerDependencies` so the build tooling federates it. The exact `2.5.1` devDependency was already in place, so the fallback copy already matches the app shell.

The openmrs rspack config builds the module federation `shared` list from `peerDependencies`. `swr` was installed but not declared as a peer, so the built entry registered no `swr` share and bundled a private copy. `useSWR` from that copy reads its own `SWRConfig` context, not the one the framework's component decorator provides, so the laboratory app has been running on SWR's stock defaults (revalidate on focus and reconnect, unlimited retries on every error) and its own cache rather than the shared one.

Verified by building and checking the remote entry, which now registers `swr`, `swr/_internal`, `swr/immutable` and `swr/infinite` at 2.5.1 like the other O3 apps. Same change as openmrs/openmrs-esm-form-builder#1347, where the dev server run against dev3 showed the forms list stop refetching on window focus once the framework's `revalidateOnFocus: false` applied.

Federating swr changes one more thing, which the first e2e run on this branch caught: `useInvalidateLabOrders` and the add-results action refreshed the order tables through the global `mutate` imported from `swr`. That function is bound to SWR's default cache, while every hook rendered under the framework's component decorator lives in the decorator's provider cache. With the private copy the two coincided, so it worked by accident. Once swr is shared, the global `mutate` reaches nothing, and the In progress and Declined tables stayed empty after pickup and reject (three identical e2e runs). The second commit takes `mutate` from `useSWRConfig()` instead, which is bound to the provider cache and is what patient-chart already does everywhere.

## Screenshots

## Related Issue

## Other

Last of four. The others are openmrs/openmrs-esm-form-builder#1347, openmrs/openmrs-esm-cohortbuilder-app#720 and openmrs/openmrs-esm-admin-tools#372.

The config table was wrong. `labTableColumns` didn't list `urgency` in its default or allowed values, and `usePreferredPatientIdentifier` wasn't there at all. The customization section told implementers to edit `routes.json`. That's not how slots get configured, so it now points at `extensionSlots` config and lists the slots we render.

We also had nothing on which fulfiller status each tab shows, what the actions do, which other frontend modules we pull workspaces and modals from, the backend requirement, or how to run against a backend other than dev3. Those are all in now, along with the rest of the scripts, e2e setup, translations, and the PR title convention.

Both screenshots predate the Add test order button and the urgency column, so they contradicted the text they sit next to. Retook them against dev3 at 2x with the default columns.

The o3-docs links in both READMEs were 404ing since the site moved under `/en-US/`. Fixed those too.

## Summary

Typing a year into the lab orders date range picker drops focus after the first digit. Each segment edit changes the orders query, and the loading skeleton was replacing the whole table, including the toolbar.

This moves the skeleton below the toolbar so the picker, status filter and search stay mounted while orders reload. The regression test checks the controls, date picker focus and search state across loaded, loading and loaded states.

Validation messages also made the picker taller than the fixed-height toolbar, pushing it up into the tabs. The toolbar now grows to contain the message, aligns the controls at the top and lets them wrap when space is limited. The date label stays aligned with the input. In the normal state this makes the toolbar 16px taller than before, from the 8px of padding above and below the controls.

## Summary

This moves linting from `.eslintrc`, `.eslintignore`, and ESLint 8 to a flat config based on [`@openmrs/eslint-config`](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-contrib-eslint-config) 2.0.0 and ESLint 9. The repo-specific rules stay in an overlay, including the three rules that replaced `ban-types`. Although the old config set `ban-types` to off, that rule no longer existed in typescript-eslint v8 and its replacements were already enforced by the recommended preset.

The dependency updater now names only the packages that actually publish a `next` tag, so it leaves the stable-only ESLint config on its declared range.

The config keeps type information for `consistent-type-exports`. The shared test and e2e rules update two matchers, move two top-level `afterEach` hooks above the tests, add two scoped `no-node-access` exceptions for Carbon's search wrapper, and remove four stale disables.

Validated with `eslint . --max-warnings 0`, `yarn typescript`, the 33 unit tests, and `prettier --check`.

body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [x] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Migrates laboratory-app's test runner from jest to vitest, aligning it with `openmrs-esm-core`, `openmrs-esm-billing-app`, and the in-flight migrations across the other O3 apps.

Changes:
- Replace `jest`, `@swc/jest`, `jest-cli`, `jest-environment-jsdom`, and `@types/jest` with `vitest`, `@vitest/coverage-v8`, `jsdom`, and `cross-env`.
- Bump `@testing-library/dom` (8.x to 10.x) and `@testing-library/jest-dom` (5.x to 6.x). The 6.x `jest-dom` is required for the `/vitest` subpath import that wires the DOM matchers into vitest's `expect`.
- Add `vitest.config.ts`. Keeps the original `jsdom` environment, aliases `.scss`/`.css` imports to `identity-obj-proxy` (the regex anchors `^.*...$` so the entire path is replaced, not just the extension), aliases `@openmrs/esm-framework` to its mock and `react-i18next` to the local `__mocks__` file, stubs `workbox-window` (pulled in transitively via `esm-react-utils`), inlines `@openmrs/*` deps so Vite processes them, and caps `fakeTimers.toFake` to exclude `queueMicrotask` (otherwise breaks React's scheduler).
- Update `tools/setup-tests.ts` to load `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest` and register `afterEach(cleanup)`; the ResizeObserver mock is unchanged.
- Convert the five test files to the vitest API: explicit imports for `describe`/`expect`/`it`/`vi` (plus `beforeEach` where used), `jest.*` swapped for `vi.*`.
- Delete `jest.config.js`.

Stacked on top of the `feat/migrate-to-rspack` branch so the rspack and vitest changes can land in sequence without re-resolving `yarn.lock` twice. Once rspack lands on `main`, please re-target this PR to `main`.

N/A — tooling change only.

N/A

All 19 tests pass locally. \`yarn lint\` and \`yarn typescript\` are green.
